Indeed, a day before the eagerly awaited northern derby against HSV, the team are sitting in a sensational sixth place. That was hardly on the cards just a few weeks ago. Bremen endured a largely difficult summer transfer window, and there were doubts about Thioune too. Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: Pakistan’s board has unveiled its new central contracts after a long delay. PCB snubs Test skipper from T20I contract A number of familiar faces have disappeared from Pakistan’s central contracts list for 2026-27, and the biggest surprises are former captains Mohammad Rizwan and Shan Masood. Opener Imam-ul-Haq has also been left out of the list that the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) released on Saturday. The announcement arrived much later than usual, since the previous set of contracts had run out on June 30. The wait ended with a revamped system, and the changes are bigger than most expected. Test skipper Babar Azam has no T20I contract this time. The batsman has often been under the scanner for his low strike rates in T20s and the recent contract list is another hammer blow to his T20I future. ODI captain Shaheen Shah Afridi sits in the ODI/T20 category, while Sahibzada Farhan, who led Pakistan in their most recent T20 Internationals, has a deal in the T20 group alone. No player has been offered a contract that covers all three formats. The board did not reveal how much each category will pay. It did hand contracts to 38 players, and most of them have landed in a newly created development category. item.title: Seville’s Passionate ‘Gran Derbi’ Divides A City Looking To The Future
item.description: Pablo Fornals of Real Betis celebrates a goal against Sevilla at the Pizjuán last November. Europa Press via Getty Images The last time Real Betis visited Sevilla’s Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán for ‘ El Gran Derbi ’, the game was stopped for more than 15 minutes. Betis won 2-0 that afternoon in November 2025, with second-half goals from Pablo Fornals and Sergi Altimira. Sevilla striker Isaac Romero was sent off and objects thrown from the stands forced the referee to halt play. On Saturday evening, at 6:30pm local time, the Seville derby goes back to Nervión. It is the 13th round of LaLiga, but in Seville nobody treats it as one game among 38. “Here in Seville, football is a way of life, like a religion,” Álvaro Valles told me in a LALIGA press event this week. The Betis goalkeeper was born just outside the city and came through the club’s academy. A rivalry older than LaLiga Sevilla were founded in 1890 while Betis came later, out of a split at Sevilla, and in 1914 a merger created Real Betis Balompié. The first Seville derby was played on October 8, 1915, and Sevilla won it 4-3, and the two side have now met 145 times in official competition. Sevilla lead the record with 66 wins, but have failed to win any of the last three. After November’s heated affair, the return game at La Cartuja in March finished 2-2, after Betis led 2-0 at half time and Alexis Sánchez and Isaac Romero brought Sevilla level. “More than three points” What sets the derby apart is that both clubs carry national weight from the same city. “These are two powerful clubs at national level, and the rivalry is huge,” Valles told international media. “Having two nationally important clubs in the city of Seville makes this match very important all over the world.” Alvaro Valles of Real Betis gestures during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD4 match between Borussia Dortmund and Real Betis Balompie at BVB Stadion Dortmund. Getty Images Valles has a useful comparison, as Betis are in the Champions League this season, and he has already played at Borussia Dortmund, with a trip to Bayern Munich to come in January. Asked how those atmospheres compare with a Seville derby, he said they are not alike. “A derby is a one-off game. I always say it doesn’t matter what form either team is in. It’s like a final,” he says. “They’re still worth three points like any other game, but against your eternal rival they’re more than three points. It’s the pride of a whole city.” He has lived the rivalry since childhood as Valles grew up in La Rinconada, left the Betis academy to make his name at UD Las Palmas, and came back to the club in 2025 after spending a year in the stands to see out his contract and ensure a move back to his boyhood club. He calls the return “a dream I had wanted to fulfil since I was a kid: playing at home, in my city, for the club of my life.” Two homes in flux The stadiums that built this rivalry are both about to change. item.title: Manchester United rival Liverpool for Italy international defender as club also informed of former midfielder's potential 2027 return
item.description: Atalanta BC v Parma Calcio - Serie A 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Manchester United are rivalling Liverpool for Italy international centre-back Giorgio Scalvini as they plan for life after Lisandro Martinez. The Old Trafford hierarchy have also been alerted to a possible 2027 reunion with former midfielder Scott McTominay amid contract talks at Napoli. Recruitment chiefs scout defensive targets According to TEAMtalk , United are carrying out detailed scouting work on Scalvini as they prepare to reinforce up front, at left-back and in central defence. The Italian has caught the eye of several recruitment departments and could become a major defensive target in 2027, either in January or next summer. That search comes as Martinez enters the final months of his deal, despite a one-year club option. Agent chief questions Barcelona interest Speculation surrounding Martinez's future has gathered pace following earlier claims from the outlet that Barcelona admire the Argentine defender, alongside reports in Spain suggesting he is open to listening to an offer from the Liga giants. However, the president of the Spanish Association of Football Agents, Pedro Bravo, has poured cold water on any potential switch to Catalonia. Addressing the transfer rumours, Bravo said: "Lisandro, as far as I'm aware, neither Deco nor [Hansi] Flick are keen on him." He added that the message coming from Flick and sporting director Deco regarding Martinez is clear: "He's a good player, but we don't like him. He doesn't fit in with us." Regardless of Barcelona's stance, Martinez's contract situation still points towards an Old Trafford exit in the near future. Scottish playmaker considers English comeback Alongside their defensive planning, the report states that former United midfielder McTominay is seriously weighing up a return to the Premier League in 2027. His previous employers have already been notified of the opportunity to bring the academy graduate back to Manchester, and club officials have not dismissed the prospect. The publication's sources believe Napoli remain hopeful of keeping the Scotland international in Serie A, with his current agreement set to expire in 18 months. Because the two parties are currently far apart in contract negotiations, intermediaries have begun pushing him towards potential landing spots in case no middle ground can be found. Injury recovery dictates winter timing Timing will play a decisive role in how United approach both pursuits over the coming months. Because Scalvini has only recently returned from injury, a January move may arrive too soon, meaning United and Liverpool will keep tracking his form before deciding when to bid. Meanwhile, McTominay's ongoing standoff in Italy will determine whether a 2027 reunion becomes a concrete option.

item.title: Stephen A. Smith says there’s one rule stopping him from running for President
item.description: Photo by Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images Sports analyst Stephen A. Smith gives an update on whether he will try to become the next US President. Over the years, Stephen A. Smith has built an impressive fan following thanks to his unfiltered takes on the NBA and NFL. So much so that Smith has now expanded his coverage to things outside of sports, including politics in the United States of America. There have been times when the ESPN analyst has contemplated running for president, but Smith has seemingly given up on that dream. Stephen A. Smith explains why he will not run for US President During a recent podcast appearance with NBA legend Kevin Garnett, Smith talked about a plethora of things. Soon, the conversation shifted to if the ESPN on-air talent wants to run for president. Well, Smith has shut the door on any possibility and it’s because of one important rule. “Listen, would I give all of this up to be the President of the United States of America? Yes, I would. Would I give it up to campaign for the president? H___ no. And according to the rules, you have to give up everything. What they say is you’ve got to give up your money because, by virtue of what I do, let me tell you this: there’s something with the FCC called ‘the equal-time rule,” Smith said. He added, “And equal time means that because of what I do and because I’m on the air all the time, the minute I announce that I’m running, I have to come off the air and give up my career and the money that comes with it. “Now, that ain’t happening, dog. That’s not happening.” Running for president doesn’t automatically mean that Smith will win the election, and if he fails, he could lose relevance among fans. After all, it has taken him decades to build his audience, and even a few months’ gap could splash cold water over his years of hard work. Read more: ‘He’s done’ – Stephen A. item.title: New Man Utd boss Pochettino sure years in USA made him ‘better coach’
item.description: FILE PHOTO - USA coach Mauricio Pochettino reacts from the touchline during the International Friendly soccer match between USA and Germany at Soldier Field. An overnight flight from Cincinnati to Manchester took Pochettino from his post-match duties after the United States’ win over Haiti in the early hours of Wednesday morning to United’s Carrington complex, where he has quickly got to work ahead of Sunday’s clash with old rivals Liverpool. Pochettino has been linked with United’s top job before but, while he takes over with the club in the bottom three having won only one Premier League match all season, the 54-year-old believes he is better placed for the Old Trafford challenge now than ever before. “Of course we were missing [club football], we were missing it a lot,” he said. “I think we are animals of the grass. We like to feel the grass, we need to smell the grass and try to help the players to improve every day. “It’s true that it’s a different job when you are in the national team, but at the same time you learn a lot, and I think we are much better coaches now, much better coaches.” Pochettino has plenty of Premier League experience with Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea, taking Tottenham to both a Champions League and League Cup final, albeit without winning either, and was also a league winner with Paris St Germain. But the man who took the United States to the last 16 of this summer’s World Cup argued the pressure at international level is just as great as in club football. “The expectation and the pressure was massive,” he said. “I remember always in SoFi (Los Angeles), our first game against Paraguay, the pressure was massive, there were more than 200 celebrity people expecting us to win and to play well and all the country was behind us. “They say when you are in the Premier League or in LaLiga or in France, OK, you feel the pressure when you manage this type of size of club. “But being there was, I promise, it was massive pressure, but we found a way to translate that pressure into energy. That success marked the high of England’s time under Steve Borthwick so far, but confidence has built again for his squad after big wins over Australia and Japan. item.title: Cummins' integrity not compromised - CA
item.description: Pat Cummins was named Australia captain in 2021 [Getty Images] Cricket Australia has "unequivocally rejected" the suggestion that captain Pat Cummins' integrity has been compromised by the sandpaper scandal. On Saturday CA gave its "unanimous support" to Cummins, and he said he would take part in the independent forum set up for players and staff. Cummins has faced claims to step down as captain after Cameron Bancroft's detailed testimony supported claims made by Usman Khawaja that the entire Australia team knew of the plan to tamper with the ball during a Test against South Africa in Cape Town in 2018. CA and Cummins met this week, with the former saying it was "determined to steward Australian cricket through this very difficult time with diligence and patience and to listen and learn". "We've expressed our support to Pat and our concern for everyone impacted by the events of the 2018 tour of South Africa," CA said. "We have learned from that experience and are proud of the team and the culture Pat and other leaders in the team have fostered over the past eight years and unequivocally reject any implication that Pat's integrity has been compromised." CA chief executive Todd Greenberg said Cummins has been an "exemplary leader" in his five years as captain. "He has consistently spoken and articulated what happened back in 2018 in his version of events. Nothing's changed. Thus, nothing's changing with our captaincy," Greenberg told BBC Sport. Greenberg acknowledged that people's version of events "directly contradict" each other but said Cummins has "not moved one inch" from his story, giving the same account now as he did when interviewed the day after the Cape Town Test in 2018. Cummins is due to lead Australia in the opening match of a four-Test series against New Zealand starting on 9 December in Perth. The pace bowler reiterated his stance that he had no involvement in or knowledge of the sandpaper plot during a 68-minute news conference last week. Cummins has said he will attend the forum that has been set up by CA for players and staff to share their version of events. "I support the forum 100%. I will be there," he said. "All of the players and staff I have spoken with are very keen to go and to have their say. "There will be a lot of difficult conversations, but that is what's needed. "Otherwise, from this point, captaining the Australian team in Perth will be my focus and priority." The row over the sandpaper saga, one of the biggest controversies in Test history, has engulfed Australian sport since Khawaja's claims emerged two weeks ago. In 2018 Bancroft was banned for nine months and captain Steve Smith and vice-captain David Warner for a year after Bancroft was caught rubbing sandpaper on the ball during the third Test at Newlands. item.title: Mika Baur’s injury presents early Celtic opportunity for Joel Van Den Berg
item.description: Mika Baur’s injury presents early Celtic opportunity for Joel Van Den Berg Martin O’Neill and the Celtic supporters have been hit with a massive blow after it was revealed that influential midfielder Mika Baur will miss up to ten weeks with an ankle ligament injury… Mika Baur ‘fouls’ Greg Kiltie of Kilmarnock (ultimately leading to Kasper Hogh’s goal being dissallowed) during the Scottish Premiership match between Celtic and Kilmarnock at Celtic Park on November 08, 2026. (Photo by Ian MacNicol/Getty Images) The German international midfielder limped off in the closing stages of the 1-0 win over Kilmarnock a fortnight ago and was forced to pull out of the German under 21 squad for their recent matches. However Celtic fans were hoping that this was no more than a knock meaning that the hugely impressive Celtic star would be back in action after the International break. However that is NOT the case and instead it is going to be around February before we see Baur back in action, although the player himself has told Martin O’Neill that he is a quick healer, so maybe that estimated return date can be brought forward a week or two. Mika Baur of Celtic passes the ball during the UEFA Europa League match between Celtic FC and Besiktas JK at Celtic Park on November 05, 2026. (Photo by Zak Mauger/Getty Images) In an update on Friday at his mainstream media conference , the Celtic manager somewhat relectantly broke the bad news: “It his ankle. He’ll be out for some considerable time. It’s a real shame. He was playing great for us. “I think there’s talk about 10 weeks, but I spoke to Mika yesterday and he’s a quick healer. There’s things that he can’t do for a while. His foot’s in the boot and stuff like this here. “I think it was a bigger injury than, for instance, that Joel van den Berg had, so it might be a couple of extra weeks.” Benjamin Nygren of Celtic is seen during the Scottish Premiership match between Celtic and Kilmarnock at Celtic Park on November 08, 2026. item.title: An Australian captain who can play for Wales in 2027
item.description: Liam Wright had to wait four years between his fifth and six caps for Australia [Getty Images] Ospreys flanker and once-Australian captain Liam Wright will be at the Principality Stadium today to watch the Wallabies take on Wales in Cardiff. Wright knows that in less than a year, it is possible he could be playing for Australia or Wales at the World Cup in the land of his birth. The 29-year-old has made six appearances for the Wallabies, but his previous game was in July 2024. So despite being capped by the Wallabies, World Rugby regulations would allow him to play for another country three years after his previous international appearance. His eligibility to switch allegiances would start next summer, and just a few months before the World Cup begins in Australia in September 2027. Wright has Welsh heritage, with his grandfather hailing from Pembroke Dock. After more than a year out of professional rugby, Wright moved 12,000 miles to join Ospreys and wants to return to the international stage. "Test rugby is what I want to get to; it's the pinnacle and where I want to play and end up again," he said. Will an international return be for Australia or Wales? Liam Wright played in the back row for Australia against Wales in July 2024 [Getty Images] Which country Wright might play for remains to be seen. When asked about potentially representing Wales, he replied: "I imagine myself playing Test rugby and wanting to do it in a gold jersey, but I'm not going to turn down opportunities anywhere. "If the door is closed for the Wallabies and I'm playing good enough and Wales do come knocking, I'd definitely explore it. "I want to get back playing Test footy [rugby] and play for the Wallabies, but fate has a weird way of working where we've landed in Wales. "I've now got to explore the heritage. I was going past Pembroke Dock the other week and stayed there in an Airbnb and explored the area a bit, which is where my grandfather's from. "Things have a funny way of working out, so I won't rule anything out." Wright will be mindful that Wales and Australia have impressive back-row resources at their disposal. Wales head coach Steve Tandy told the Scrum V podcast in October he had not talked to Wright, who met up with the Australian camp in Cardiff this week. Australia head coach Les Kiss knows Wright well from their Queensland days. "We will always keep an eye on someone of his calibre," said Kiss. "The big thing for Liam was getting back into the game, and I've worked closely with him at the Reds for a number of years. "He was in that gym, in the physio room, throwing everything to get that shoulder right. "I loved the look in his eyes this week. He looked happy again, getting out there, plying his trade and loving the sense of living in a different environment. "I was happy to catch up with him and see how he feels good about himself again." item.title: Monza want €40m for Gustavo Varela, but is he worth it?
item.description: Monza want €40m for Gustavo Varela, but is he worth it? Serie A has several underdog stories blossoming this season on both team and player levels and is all the more worthwhile for it. One such story is of Gustavo Varela, who despite being in his debut season in Italy already looks like a man on a mission. Having scored just seven goals last season in 33 appearances while on loan at Gil Vicente from Benfica, the 21-year-old already has 11 goals in 11 outings this term. These are numbers few were expecting, that too for a team not expected to have a great campaign. Monza are again looking down the barrel, and between their early-season slump and several of their counterparts looking keen to at least put up a fight, things are not looking good for the Brianzoli. But Varela is unquestionably a shining light. Even if he doesn’t manage to help keep Monza up, he is turning enough heads to be able to earn himself a move and not have to try his luck in Serie B. Some even believe a mid-season switch to not be out of question. It would make sense if Monza were to capitalise on his hype knowing they might go down anyway, and there’s previous for this. But is it too soon for Varela? Is he really already worth €40 million. Despite market valuations, the price of a player comes down to however much the buying party is willing to conjure up. And while there are several success stories featuring players who move early and thrive, there are several others — often more frequent — of players who move too early and for too lofty a price tag which they never manage to justify. In recent years alone there are several cautionary tales. Krzysztof Piątek, case in point, looked like the next great striker of his generation before moving to Milan after just half a season with Genoa, and while his numbers mostly remain respectable, the now Al-Duhail man never reached the heights that were expected of him during his short stint at the Marassi. Similarly, Juan Manuel Iturbe, a darling of the video game folk, arrived at Roma amid much fanfare before his career plateaued. After struggling in Europe, he has gone on to have a respectable career in the Americas and is currently at his boyhood club, Cerro Porteño. In fact, one could even argue that Juventus that did not quite get what they were hoping for when they splurged €70 million on Dušan Vlahović to pry him away from Fiorentina in January 2022. All that said, the fact of the matter remains that the current market is a fidgeting, impatient one. item.description: Al Ahli vs Al Nassr : Saudi Pro League - Getty Images Sport Crystal Palace are considering a January swoop for Al-Ahli striker Ivan Toney as new boss Thomas Frank looks to reunite with his former forward. Euro ambitions drive return hopes According to talkSPORT , Palace have identified Toney as a winter option after promising Frank the resources needed to strengthen a squad rooted to the foot of the table . Having previously worked under the Danish coach at Brentford, the forward is keen to boost his chances of making England's Euro 2028 squad. Those international hopes recently took a knock when he failed to move a court date clashing with the tournament . Prolific spell highlights goalscoring pedigree Toney left Brentford for Saudi Arabia in a £40 million transfer during the summer of 2024 , departing west London with a proven top-flight record of 36 goals in 85 Premier League appearances. Since arriving at Al-Ahli, his output in front of goal has become even more formidable across both domestic and continental competition. The 30-year-old has amassed 87 goals in just 109 outings in all competitions for the Saudi Pro League side, playing a central role in helping them lift back-to-back AFC Champions League Elite titles. His blistering form has continued into the current campaign, where he has already registered 15 goals in 16 appearances, including 14 strikes in 10 league matches to top the division's scoring charts. Selhurst Park attack desperately struggles That clinical edge stands in stark contrast to Palace's glaring issues in the final third this season. item.description: Harden joined the Cavaliers in February after three years with the Los Angeles Clippers [Getty Images] James Harden scored 51 points to move third on the all-time list for 50-point NBA games as the Cleveland Cavaliers beat the Indiana Pacers 128-119 in the NBA Cup. The 37-year-old made all 14 of his free throws as his recorded his 26th 50-point game to move above the legendary Kobe Bryant. Harden, who also made six rebounds and provided six assists at Rocket Arena in Cleveland, had not passed 50 points since scoring 55 for the Los Angeles Clippers in November 2025. Legendary centre Wilt Chamberlain holds the NBA record ⁠with 118 50-point games, while Michael Jordan is second with 31. "When you talk about just basketball, obviously Wilt was elite, but you got Mike and Kobe - shooting guard position, the best to ever do it - so just to be in that conversation, it's very humbling and it's definitely special," said an emotional Harden. Aged 37 years and 86 days, he is the fourth oldest player to score 50 points in a game. "What excites me a lot is even being in my 18th year learning how to still be impactful," said Harden, the ninth highest scorer in NBA history with 29,633 points. "It's easy when you're young - 23, 24, you run around, you jump high and can move fast and get by. Now it's like, you're not as fast. "That's the evolution of James Harden and figuring that out. "Tonight was a confidence-booster that I can do it at a high level still." The Cavaliers travel to the Chicago Bulls in the NBA on Tuesday.

item.title: Harry Kane out for a ‘few months’ as Bayern Munich confirm ankle ligament tear
item.description: Harry Kane faces the "next few months" on the sidelines after suffering a torn left ankle ligament during Bayern Munich ’s 1-1 draw against Cologne on Friday. The injury occurred when Cologne defender Joel Schmied intercepted Michael Olise’s low cross at the back post, clattering into the Ballon d’Or winner’s left leg on the follow-through. Though the England captain got back to his feet after treatment, he was unable to continue and hobbled off the pitch accompanied by two physios. Following an assessment by the club’s medical team, Bayern confirmed Kane had sustained a torn syndesmotic ligament and "will therefore be sidelined for the next few months". It is a major setback for Kane, who won the Ballon d’Or last month and then became the most-capped England men’s player of all time last week, surpassing the previous record held by Peter Shilton. Kane received treatment but was unable to continue on Friday night (Getty) Kane scored 73 goals last season to earn the Ballon d’Or and had made a flying start to the current campaign, registering 10 goals and 10 assists in 16 games for Bayern across all competitions. He also scored eight goals in six Nations League games to help England top their group as he took his overall international tally to 93 goals in 127 caps. England learned on Friday that they will face Norway in the Nations League quarter-finals, which will be a rematch of the two teams meeting at the same stage of the World Cup back in July. Thomas Tuchel’s side won that game 2-1 thanks to a brace from Jude Bellingham, and the two-legged quarter-final will be played in late March. Kane will hope that he is back in time for that tie, but Bayern’s statement indicates that he will not be seen on the pitch for the remainder of 2026 or the early weeks of 2027. Kane’s injury is a real blow for Bayern (Tom Weller/PA) Bayern also suffered another injury blow on Friday night as Michael Olise failed to return for the second half. The club issued an update on Olise’s condition after the game. The statement read: “Michael Olise has been diagnosed with a contusion of the foot. The French attacking player will receive treatment over the coming days.”

item.title: B1G volleyball tournament brings Illinois freshman back to hometown roots
item.description: FISHERS — The entirety of Friday has been a surreal experience for Hamilton Southeastern High School grad Madi Miles. Now an outside hitter for the Illinois volleyball team, the 6-1 freshman is back in her hometown for the inaugural Big Ten volleyball tournament, which began this weekend at the Fishers Event Center. The Illini made the two-hour bus ride from Champaign on Friday morning, allowing Miles to take in all the familiar sights as they headed to the venue. That in itself was a "weird" and "crazy" experience, Miles said. And then they arrived at the facility. The 2025 Indiana Miss Volleyball finalist estimates she ran into at least five people she knew while walking around the events center, the encounters ranging from former teachers and the dad of former high school teammate Jasmine Daniels, to Fishers mayor Scott Fadness and former HSE athletic director Jim Self, who grabbed a photo with Miles before the team departed for practice. "It's been really cool seeing all the familiar faces — and that's just today," Miles said. "We don't even play (tonight), so I can't wait to see what Saturday's going to be like." As the regular season began winding down, Miles' high school coach, Jason Young, was pushing for Hamilton Southeastern to host Illini practices for the duration of their stay. "My mom was in contact with him and keeping me updated," she laughed. "It's so weird being back," Miles later added. The entire team strolled the athletic corridor, checking out pictures of their teammate from her days as a two-time Class 4A state champion with the powerhouse Royals. Inside the gym, the video boards displayed a graphic welcoming Miles home with her two most recent team photos and the message "Once a Royal, always a Royal." And, yes, the team made sure to get a photo with the signage before starting practice. "My teammates are amazing," Miles said. "They've been really helping me and pushing me." Those teammates, she continued, have helped fuel her recent run of success, maintaining trust in her and feeding her balls in spots where they know she can be successful. To wit, Miles racked up 106 kills over an eight-match stretch between October and November, then collected six kills, two digs and two blocks in the regular-season finale at Iowa. item.title: United States expected to host 2028 Copa America in second consecutive edition on American soil
item.description: Argentina v Colombia - CONMEBOL Copa America USA 2024: Final - Getty Images Sport Organisers are formalising plans for the United States to stage the 2028 Copa America, with an official announcement anticipated soon. The tournament will mark the second straight edition of South America's premier international competition held on American soil. Confederations finalise joint hosting talks According to The Athletic , all parties now expect the 2028 competition to return to the US following extensive discussions between CONMEBOL and CONCACAF that began in December 2025. Anonymous sources confirmed the host nation is not yet finalised, while Brazilian publication Globo also reported on Friday night that an announcement is imminent. Once confirmed, the US will have hosted three of the last five editions between 2016 and 2028. Commercial success outweighs previous controversies When the two confederations jointly organised the 2024 tournament, all 10 South American nations were joined by six CONCACAF guests: the US, Mexico, Canada, Panama, Costa Rica and Jamaica. Over 1.5 million supporters attended the 16-team event, which generated the majority of CONMEBOL's $319 million in national team competition revenue that year. However, the 2024 edition also drew scrutiny. Players and coaches criticised stadium playing surfaces, while Argentina's 1-0 final win over Colombia at Miami's Hard Rock Stadium was delayed by roughly 80 minutes due to dangerous crowd issues. The hosts also exited at the group stage, leading Gregg Berhalter to be replaced by Mauricio Pochettino, who coached the team at the World Cup before joining Manchester United . Packed calendar shapes summer scheduling The report states that CONCACAF nations will again have a pathway to qualify in 2028, though the exact number of spots and qualification process remain unspecified. Scheduling will require careful coordination because Los Angeles hosts the Summer Olympics starting on July 14, 2028, the exact calendar date of the 2024 final, with the US football team set to compete under coach Steve Cherundolo. Fortunately, domestic league clashes should be avoided, as Major League Soccer switches to a European-style calendar from 2027-28, ending campaigns in late May. The tournament extends a remarkable run of major events in the US, following the 2025 Club World Cup, the 2026 World Cup, and a joint bid with Mexico, Jamaica and Costa Rica for the 2031 Women's World Cup. Formal confirmation awaits confederation decision Formal confirmation of the 2028 hosts is expected shortly, though a CONMEBOL press officer noted no official statement had yet been received and CONCACAF declined to comment. Meanwhile, the CONMEBOL council met on Friday to reiterate its backing for FIFA president Gianni Infantino ahead of upcoming elections. Next week will also see the joint 2031 Women's World Cup hosting bid officially confirmed.

item.description: Motorsport photo Rashid Al Dhaheri took victory in the Macau Grand Prix qualification race after jumping polesitter Alex Ninovic at the start and resisting a final-lap attack from Mattia Colnaghi. Rodin racer Ninovic had set the pace during a heavily disrupted opening qualifying session on Thursday that featured five red flags, before Friday's Q2 was rain-affected, but the Australian did not make a great launch from pole and was instantly under pressure from Al Dhaheri. The R-ace GP driver - who finished fourth in the Formula Regional European Championship standings this year - had grabbed the lead before the first turn, while Red Bull Junior Colnaghi demoted Ninovic to third on the run to Lisboa. Colnaghi, who looked rapid in first practice but could not replicate that during the chaotic qualifying, then set about closing the gap to Al Dhaheri. This was 1.1 seconds by the end of the first tour and continued to fluctuate between just below and just over a second for much of the contest. But Colnaghi suddenly closed to within half a second on the penultimate tour and mounted an attack into Lisboa for the final time but was never able to draw alongside his rival. MP Motorsport competitor Colnaghi therefore had to settle for a front-row start for Sunday's main race, finishing just 0.251s behind across the line. Mattia Colnaghi Mattia Colnaghi Ninovic drifted away from the lead duo to end up 3s back from Al Dhaheri but last year's GB3 champion was never under pressure for third, while Pinnacle Motorsport driver Enzo Deligny was fourth. Williams junior Kean Nakamura-Berta was fifth for much of the race but was passed by Indy NXT frontrunner Tymek Kucharczyk in the closing stages. For all the drama during qualifying, the race was relatively incident-free with the only significant clash coming on the third lap when Taito Kato tagged Kabir Anurag out of Lisboa, which damaged the suspension on the latter's RPM machine. Although this forced Anurag to stop on track, his car was quickly cleared without need for a caution. Also in strife was Sebastian Wheldon, who pulled into the pits at mid-distance having struggled at the wheel of a new chassis after his original car split in two pieces following a crash in the Esses that caused one of the multiple qualifying stoppages. item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. But he wasn’t the right fit for the Crew in the post-Nancy era. The Crew turned to Courtois, a former Crew academy and MLS Next Pro coach who continued the idea first expressed on the field so successfully by Nancy’s teams. The squad might not have been the entirely right squad, either. Tall turned to a scouting network led by Mark Nichols, bringing in a proven MLS veteran in Santi Rodriguez, Chile national team forward Gonzalo Tapia, securing a loan deal for Moroccan winger Anass Zaroury and signing designated player Brais Mendez, a Spanish attacker whose arrival from Real Sociedad brought to mind that of Cucho Hernandez. While Mendez is at a different stage of his carer than Hernandez was, he turned into a star in Columbus, showing his full potential in MLS after frustrating stints with Watford and loans in Huseca, Mallorca and Getafe. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. Gotham was unbeaten in its past 13 matches at Sports Illustrated, which is operated by the Red Bulls of MLS. Croix Bethune, left, celebrates scoring a goal with Kansas City Current teammate Lo’eau LaBonta during an NWSL playoff match in New York, Nov. 15, 2026. Getty Images “I think that’s also part of the sadness,” head coach Juan Carlos Amorós said. “I think we never know what would have happened if we played on a good pitch. I think it was the right decision to come here. I think the pitch in the other stadium was unfortunately unplayable.” Tickets for the semifinal were reallotted and grabbed up in a hurry, while Gotham officials ground on the logistics of moving their game-day operations. “Obviously not ideal we had to change stadiums, but … I think that’s really awesome to come into a new environment, a new stadium, you have to adapt, you have to make sure you can bring that energy and our supporters did that tonight and that’s incredible,” Gotham midfielder Savannah McCaskill said. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.description: Seattle Reign FC defender Phoebe McClernon, left, defends Gotham FC forward Guro Reiten during an NWSL playoff game in Harrison, N.J., Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. For the first time in franchise history, Gotham FC is set to host its semifinal match next weekend. But there’s an unfortunate twist. Gotham’s semifinal match against the Kansas City Current won’t be played at the club’s typical stomping grounds in Harrison, New Jersey. Instead, Gotham agreed to move Sunday’s match to Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island for better playing surface quality. “This was an extremely difficult decision, and one we did not take lightly,” Gotham president of soccer operations Yael Averbuch West said in a letter to fans. “After thoughtful consultation with coach Juan Carlos Amorós, our team captains, and our ownership, we felt it was important to prioritize a playing surface that appropriately allows our athletes to perform at their best. Lev Radin/Shutterstock Gotham is a tenant of Major League Soccer’s Red Bull New York at Sports Illustrated Stadium. The Red Bulls are scheduled to play an exhibition game there Saturday night, exacerbating concerns about the field quality. The state of Sports Illustrated Stadium’s pitch has been a cause for concern over the past two weeks. ESPN reported the NWSL fined Gotham $10,000 for poor field conditions during last week’s regular-season finale, after which the club was awarded its first league Shield. item.title: NYCFC fires head coach Pascal Jansen after second-half collapse
item.description: NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. New York City FC will be looking for a new head coach this offseason. Less than 24 hours after the club played its final match of the 2026 season, NYCFC announced that it fired head coach Pascal Jansen following a disappointing campaign that saw the club miss the playoffs for only the third time in its 12-year history. NYCFC went through an ugly 2026 season, finishing 11th in the Eastern Conference and being knocked out of playoff contention before the club even reached its Decision Day matchup with D.C. United on Saturday. The rough season was highlighted by the massive second-half collapse NYCFC went through following the World Cup break, posting a 5W-8D-6L record and sliding from eighth place to 11th. Jansen was informed of the decision by the club’s front office on Sunday morning and ultimately the decision to move on from him as head coach came down to the “failure of making playoffs” following a “disappointing season,” a source told The Post. NYCFC has fired head coach Pascal Jansen. The club views this next year as a “crucial point in franchise history” and the feeling is that NYCFC wants to make sure it has “the right leadership in place,” the source added. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month. item.title: On MLS Decision Day, D.C. United faces a familiar reality: Another season of failure
item.description: WASHINGTON — All around Major League Soccer , from Montreal to Miami and Seattle to San Diego, Saturday was Decision Day — the last act in an 8½-month production. While three playoff berths were in the balance, teams with guaranteed spots sought to improve their place. It's a day marked by desperation, scoreboard-watching and playoff-planning. At Audi Field, however, Decision Day felt more like Derision Day. For the seventh consecutive year, D.C. United, once a showpiece of a blossoming league, has no playoff plans — a near impossibility in a league that distributes postseason passes like a guy on a New York street corner handing out flyers for discount mattresses. Only Toronto FC's eight-year rut, starting with its 2007 expansion campaign, lasted longer. United wasn't even in the mix on Decision Day, its fate having been decided 10 days earlier. The lowly finale was against another failed side, New York City FC, which claimed a 1-0 victory on a late goal. While 2026 was an anomaly for the New Yorkers, it was the norm in the nation's capital. D.C. added another sad chapter to a rotten story under an ownership group, led by Jason Levien and Steve Kaplan, that has dragged the organization into irrelevance in not just the prospering league but in the local market and the ascending sport. The public-address announcer introduces the team as "your four-time MLS Cup champions," but he's been saying that for a long time. Given the league's evolution, it feels even longer. United's last title, in 2004, came in a 10-team operation — one-third the current landscape. Since then, 13 different clubs have hoisted the trophy. Less than two miles north of Audi Field, the U.S. Capitol witnessed a historic sea change Tuesday with a political wave that swept the ruling party out of office. Local soccer fans have had no such luck with those in power at Audi Field. Under the current regime … United hasn't won a playoff game in 11 years and hasn't advanced to the conference finals in 14. Twelve years have passed since it won at least half its 34 matches. United's only trophy in recent memory was the 2013 U.S. Open Cup, which came amid a horrific, three-win regular season. D.C. is on its fourth head coach since Ben Olsen's departure in late 2020 and its second head of soccer operations in four years. The current director, Erkut Sogut — an agent best known for representing former German star Mesut Özil — was hired last fall without any experience working for a team. Another goal conceded, another season to forget. Keisuke Kurokawa's frustration summed up D.C. United's latest disappointing chapter. Scott Taetsch via Getty Images United remains one of three MLS organizations without a developmental team bridging the youth academy to the first team. item.title: How the final standings look after dramatic MLS Decision Day 📊
item.description: We've got a dramatic day of MLS action on offer today as the 2026 regular season comes to an end. How the final standings look after dramatic MLS Decision Day 📊 With all games in the the respective conferences kicking off at the same time, we should get some epic finishes around the East and West. Here is how it all shaped out. Western Conference Vancouver came into the day having already wrapped up top spot in the conference, but their win in Montréal meant they set single-season club records in both points (64) and wins (19). Meanwhile, coming into the night there were six teams fighting for three remaining playoff spots — those spots fell to Portland (7th), Seattle (8th), and Real Salt Lake (9th), with the latter two facing off in the play-in match. An impressive win from Dallas and a defeat for San Jose means the Texas outfit wrapped up second place in the conference. And finally, the LA Galaxy saw their campaign in bitter fashion, starting the night in control of 7th place, but finishing 11th and out of the playoffs after a defeat in Salt Lake City. Eastern Conference Most notably, Nashville SC set a new MLS regular season points record after dispatching Cincinnati this afternoon. Nashville's 77 points from 23 wins and eight draws sees them eclipse Inter Miami's record of 74 points. In the playoff race, a late win for Columbus in Chicago sent Antoine Griezmann and Orlando City into the play-in match, and the Crew into the top-seven in dramatic fashion. Elsewhere, Inter Miami let a 3-0 lead slip against Charlotte, who came roaring back to snatch a point. Heading into the playoffs, Miami have only won just one of their last three matches.
